accuracy.evidence: Checked against DfE Development Matters (2023) and the EYFS statutory framework: the Characteristics of Effective Learning name active learning (keeping on trying when they encounter difficulties) and creating and thinking critically (changing strategy as needed), and the ELGs Self-Regulation and Managing Self include perseverance in the face of challenge. Terms monitoring, self-regulation, strategy and help-seeking follow the EEF Metacognition and Self-Regulated Learning guidance report (2021). The safety exception (high shelf, ask at once) matches standard early years safeguarding advice.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented early slips: reading difficulty as lack of ability (prediction 1 'Kit is bad at towers', challenge tag bad), repeating the same failed move with more force (block prediction 'Push the same way, harder', tags same), rushing when a task is hard (bee prediction 'Go really fast', Zoom fast button, tag rush), hiding being stuck (tag hide), treating help-seeking as giving up (zip card, tag never) and asking before trying for something the child can do (sock and wobbly line cards go to Try again).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagtrick models noticing and choosing a strategy: clue cards for task difficulty, a speech drop onto Kit, a speed-sensitive bee steered along a twisty lane that bumps when the pointer moves too fast, a block that only fits after it is rotated, and a two-basket try-again or ask sort. flagstick is finishing a job, flagtry is persistence over days, flagbrave is trying new things and flagoops is analysing mistakes; the shingle gate passed against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Checked by driving the lab: a real slow mouse drag along the iPhone 13 path got the bee home in both rounds, while a fast swipe or the Zoom fast button bumps it back to the last checkpoint, so the child discovers that slowing down works. The block bumps on each push until it is turned, and the second bump says the same way will not help, so the new-way rule is found by doing. Done messages state the rule only after the rounds are finished.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: Kit is bad at towers versus the job is tricky (the sign cards show tricky is a clue), go really fast on the twisty path (Zoom fast bumps the bee), and push the same way harder (the block bumps every time until turned). A.reveal quotes the child's guess in the done message.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating challenge questions with ten tagged wrong answers, each with its own fix: bad (tricky is not bad at it), throw, rush, eyes (you need to look), same (change something: turn it), quit, bang (that could break it, ask), never (grown-ups like to help), hide (nobody can help). In-lab mistakes also explain, for example the sock card in Ask a grown-up says turn it the right way, you can do this one.

readability.evidence: Kid text scores well under the family kid limit with two- to eight-word sentences (Tricky does not mean you are bad at it. It means you are learning.) and lab text uses words a parent can read aloud; adult text scores about grade 8.4, under the family adult limit, while naming metacognition, monitoring, self-regulation, strategy, help-seeking, the EYFS Characteristics of Effective Learning and the ELGs.

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passed and explanation overlap with Persisting when it's hard, Having a go at something new and Learning from mistakes is under 12 percent. Each kid paragraph does one job (notice the signs, say it, slow down or try a new way, ask), and the adult paragraphs give the curriculum home, a glossary, three named mistakes with a caution about rescuing too soon, and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px Android dark and iPhone 13 light: the six sign cards sit two to a row at about 110 px tall with a large emoji, the three speech bubbles are full-width 60 px rows, the green bee lane is about 30 px wide with the bee and flower clear of the edges, the block hole and piece are large, and the six job cards plus two baskets fit with two-line labels that do not clip.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark on desktop and iPhone 13, no console or page errors, all 5 Show me tasks completed and the challenge showed. Every canvas action has a button twin (each sign card, each speech bubble, Slow step and Zoom fast, Turn it and Push it in, Pick a card and both baskets), touch targets use the young 56 px buttons, and the canvas aria-label speaks each result, such as Too fast! The bee bumped.
